titulo: Southwest Airlines (Feb 2025): $2.9 billion to shareholders, about 1,750 jobs cut. The math.
descripcion:
From the archive: Feb 2025. Not today's news.
Southwest Airlines, Feb 17, 2025 (Jordan, press release): "This decision is unprecedented in our 53-year history"
Southwest's CEO announced on Feb. 17, 2025 a reduction of approximately 1,750 employee roles, 15% of its corporate positions. The shareholder figure is from Southwest's 2025 Form 10-K.

Same year: $2.9 billion to shareholders, 2025, company-wide. $399 million of dividends and $2.6 billion of accelerated share repurchases during 2025, company-wide (Form 10-K).
The math: $2.9 billion to shareholders (2025) ÷ about 1,750 job cuts = about $1.6 million to shareholders per job cut.
This is a ratio, not a payment and not a cause: the total returned to shareholders divided by the job count. The $2.9 billion is what Southwest says it returned to shareholders in 2025, company-wide: $399 million in dividends and $2.6 billion in an accelerated share repurchase. The 1,750 roles are about 15% of corporate positions, per the 8-K. We are not saying one paid for the other.

Unprecedented in its history. Here is the shareholder column. (Our take.)

Sources:
- SEC EDGAR · Southwest Airlines, Feb 18, 2025: «“This decision is unprecedented in our 53-year history, and change requires that we make difficult decisions.» https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/92380/000119312525028035/d907526dex991.htm
- SEC EDGAR · Southwest Airlines, Feb 1, 2026: «returning $2.9 billion to Shareholders through $399 million in dividend payments and $2.6 billion through accelerated share repurchase» https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/92380/000009238026000004/luv-20251231.htm
